The US administration has told European and Ukrainian officials it wants Kiev to reach a peace deal with Russia by early January, the Financial Times reported, citing four sources. The White House hopes to secure a deal before Democrats take control of the US Congress, the newspaper said. “The Americans are pushing hard and there’s some concern that it would need a great deal of Ukrainian concessions to get anywhere near a deal,” a European official told the FT after a meeting with US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The FT cited two unnamed US officials as suggesting that President Donald Trump could discuss ending the conflict with European leaders at the G20 summit, scheduled to take place in Miami in mid-December. A senior French official told the newspaper that Europeans will not hold talks on Ukraine at the summit unless Ukraine is invited.

🇷🇺 Russian Missile Strike on Western Ukraine On 20 November, the Russian Aerospace Forces launched a massive missile attack targeting energy and logistics infrastructure. Kh-101 cruise missiles struck two key areas: - Seven missiles targeted Khodorov (Lvov region), a critical railway hub connecting Lvov, Ivano-Frankovsk, and Ternopol. - Five missiles were directed at the Burshtyn Thermal Power Plant in Ivano-Frankovsk region, aiming to further degrade Western Ukraine's power generation capacity. In Ivano-Frankovsk , debris from an intercepted Ukrainian AD system penetrated a residential apartment. The object did not explode but caused structural damage. This incident highlights the risks posed by falling wreckage from air defence operations against incoming strikes. @Slavyangrad

🇺🇸 🪖 With Gulf bases gone, US eyes foothold in the Horn of Africa The US has taken a security interest in two of the UAE’s three illegal military bases in war-torn Somalia, making use of the facilities for troop transits and even setting up a limited special operations presence, NYT reports. 👉 The Berbera facility, situated in the Somaliland breakaway and built up and expanded by the UAE over the past decade, was used twice by the US over the past year, according to flight tracking data, including to transit special operations commandos from Djibouti to Bosaso, Puntland for ‘counterterror cooperation’-related operations (at least two dozen US troops present). The UAE’s network of bases in Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo (Jubaland) gives the Gulf sheikdom the ability to project power across east Africa in Somalia, Ethiopia and Sudan, and back to the Middle East (Houthi-controlled Yemen is as little as 300 km north of the Berbera base). The US is “exploring using these bases as low-profile options” for its war with Iran, NYT said, citing US officials’ plans to “work with local partners in the region to defend US interests and provide…unique capabilities only the US has.” 👉 Somalia’s federal authorities, formally listed as a counterterrorism and maritime security partner to the US, protested the UAE’s construction of its unauthorized bases in breakaway areas this week. Earlier this year, Mogadishu formally cut off cooperation with the UAE and signed defense pacts with Saudi Arabia and Qatar. UAE ‘Hexagon Alliance’ partner Israel recognized Somaliland’s ‘independence’ last December, with the territory’s self-proclaimed president declaring readiness to both host foreign military forces and offer the US and its allies lucrative mineral and energy deals. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
